title: Prophylactic peritoneal fenestration with resorbable Vicryl mesh to reduce symptomatic lymphoceles after primary kidney transplantation: a confirmatory, monocentric, single-blind, randomized controlled superiority trial
summary: After a kidney transplant, tissue fluid can collect near the new kidney. Such fluid collections are common. Some cause no symptoms, others press on the new kidney or on blood vessels and then need treatment, for example draining the fluid through a thin tube, a procedure by the radiology department, or another operation. With this study we want to find out whether such fluid collections that need treatment can be prevented if, during the transplant operation, a small window is additionally made in the abdominal lining and held open with a mesh made of self-dissolving suture material. Through this window the fluid can drain into the abdominal cavity, where the body absorbs it. The mesh dissolves by itself after about three months and leaves no foreign material behind. Adults receiving a kidney transplant at Münster University Hospital take part in the study. All receive the transplant as usual. Chance decides whether someone additionally receives the mesh window or not. Participants are not told which group they are in. During the six months after the operation, the usual follow-up visits are used to record whether a fluid collection needing treatment has occurred. No additional examinations or visits are required.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients with an indication for primary kidney transplantation from a living or deceased donor are included. Prerequisites are written informed consent after medical information according to ICH-GCP, capacity to consent, and willingness to comply with the six-month follow-up.
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded are patients with relevant previous surgery in the ipsilateral iliac fossa, with simultaneous pancreas, liver or multivisceral organ transplantation, with known allergy or intolerance to polyglactin 910 (Vicryl), with reduced capacity to consent, and with participation in another interventional trial that could influence the primary outcomes. Pregnant and breastfeeding women are not included.
